concept.body: Three links bind the ratios. Quotient: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ. Pythagorean: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 (from a² + b² = c² divided by c²) — subtract the SQUARE, then take the root. Cofunction: sin θ = cos(90° − θ). Given any one ratio of an acute angle, the identities produce the rest.

explanationVariants: sin²θ = 1 − 0.8² = 0.36, so sin θ = 0.6 — the 3-4-5 family.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.2 = 1 − 0.8 subtracts the ratio itself — the identity subtracts its SQUARE: 1 − 0.64 = 0.36, then √0.36 = 0.6.
0.36 is sin²θ — one step short. Take the square root: 0.6.

steps.body: The three ratios aren't three strangers — they're one family. Divide sine by cosine: (opp/hyp) ÷ (adj/hyp) — the hypotenuses cancel — leaving opp/adj. That's tangent: **tan θ = sin θ / cos θ**, at every angle. Check it on 3-4-5: (3/5) ÷ (4/5) = 3/4. ✓

explanationVariants: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ = 0.6 ÷ 0.8 = 0.75 — matching 3/4 read straight off the legs.

widget.prompt: sin θ = 0.6 and cos θ = 0.8. Use the quotient identity to find tan θ.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.48 = 0.6 × 0.8 multiplies the ratios — the identity DIVIDES: sin/cos = 0.6/0.8 = 0.75.
1.33 ≈ 0.8/0.6 divides the wrong way — that's cos/sin, the tangent of the OTHER angle. sin/cos = 0.75.
0.2 = 0.8 − 0.6 subtracts. Tangent is a QUOTIENT of the two: 0.6 ÷ 0.8 = 0.75.

steps.body: A deeper link comes from Pythagoras. Divide a² + b² = c² through by c²: (a/c)² + (b/c)² = 1. But a/c and b/c ARE the sine and cosine — so **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1** for every angle. On 3-4-5: 0.36 + 0.64 = 1. ✓ Know one ratio and the identity surrenders the other.

explanationVariants: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ = 1 − (5/13)² = 144/169, so cos θ = 12/13 ≈ 0.9231 — the 5-12-13 triple in disguise.
sin θ = 5/13 puts us in a 5-12-13 triangle: adjacent 12, so cos θ = 12/13 ≈ 0.9231.

widget.prompt: An acute angle has sin θ = 5/13. Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to find cos θ (4 decimals).

commonErrors.feedback: 0.6154 = 1 − 5/13 subtracts the RATIOS — the identity subtracts their SQUARES: 1 − 25/169 = 144/169, then take the root: ≈ 0.9231.
0.4167 = 5/12 is tan θ, the leg-to-leg ratio. Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse: 12/13 ≈ 0.9231.
0.8521 = 144/169 stops at cos²θ. Take the square root: √(144/169) = 12/13 ≈ 0.9231.

steps.body: And the cofunction pattern from Chapter 2, now in full: the two acute angles are complements, and each one's opposite is the other's adjacent. So **sin θ = cos(90° − θ)** and cos θ = sin(90° − θ). That's why the names pair up: cosine literally means “sine of the complement.”

widget.prompt: At the starting 20°, note what the opp/hyp card reads. Now drag until the adj/hyp card shows that same number — and see which angle you had to travel to.
widget.scaleFeedback: Resize the triangle before checking. The claim is that sin 20° and cos 70° are the same NUMBER, so it matters that neither one moved when the lengths did.
widget.successFeedback: 70°. adj/hyp here reads 0.342, which is exactly what opp/hyp read back at 20° — so cos 70° = sin 20°, with no calculator anywhere. The two angles add to 90°: in one right triangle the two acute corners disagree about which leg is 'opposite', so sine at one seat is cosine at the other.
widget.lowFeedback: adj/hyp has dropped below 0.342. Cosine SHRINKS as the angle opens, so you have gone past 70° — bring the angle back down.
widget.highFeedback: adj/hyp is still above 0.342. Cosine falls as the angle grows, so keep opening the angle toward the partner of 20°.

predict.prompt: Somewhere between 10° and 80° there is an angle whose adj/hyp equals sin 20°. Where?

options.label: At 70° — the angle that completes 20° to a right angle
Nowhere; sine and cosine never agree

predict.reveal: At 70°. The two acute angles of a right triangle sum to 90°, and they share the same three sides — the leg that is 'opposite' from one corner is 'adjacent' from the other. That swap is the whole content of the cofunction rule.

widget.prompt: A classmate claims sin θ = 0.9 and cos θ = 0.5 for the same acute angle. Quickest disproof?

options.label: 0.9² + 0.5² = 1.06 ≠ 1, violating sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
options.feedback: The Pythagorean identity is a hard constraint — 1.06 overshoots 1, so no angle carries this pair.

options.label: Both values would need to be under 0.5
options.feedback: There's no half-cap on the ratios — sin 60° ≈ 0.87 is fine. The real test is the squares summing to 1: here they hit 1.06.

options.label: Sine can never exceed cosine
options.feedback: Past 45°, sine exceeds cosine legitimately. The disproof is the identity: 0.81 + 0.25 = 1.06 ≠ 1.

options.label: You can't disprove it without knowing θ
options.feedback: That's the identity's power — it binds EVERY θ. Since 0.81 + 0.25 ≠ 1, no angle exists, no lookup needed.

explanationVariants: cos 34° = sin(90° − 34°) = sin 56°, so the blank is 56.
The complement of 34° is 56°; cosine of one equals sine of the other.

widget.prompt: Fill in the blank: cos 34° = sin(____°).

commonErrors.feedback: sin 34° ≠ cos 34° (they only meet at 45°). The swap crosses to the COMPLEMENT: 90 − 34 = 56.
146 = 180 − 34 uses the supplement — cofunctions run on complements: 90 − 34 = 56.

hints: First recover cos θ from the Pythagorean identity: cos²θ = 1 − 0.28².
Then the quotient identity: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ = 0.28 ÷ 0.96.
explanationVariants: Two identities in a row: Pythagorean for cosine (0.96), quotient for tangent (≈ 0.2917).

widget.prompt: sin θ = 0.28 (acute θ). Find tan θ to 4 decimals — no inverse-trig keys allowed.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.72 = 1 − 0.28 subtracts ratios instead of SQUARES. cos θ = √(1 − 0.0784) = 0.96, then 0.28/0.96 ≈ 0.2917.
0.2688 = 0.28 × 0.96 multiplies at the last step — tangent DIVIDES sine by cosine: ≈ 0.2917.
3.4286 ≈ 0.96/0.28 divides upside-down — that's the other angle's tangent. sin/cos = 0.28/0.96 ≈ 0.2917.

takeaways: Quotient: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ — the hypotenuses cancel.
Pythagorean: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 — one ratio determines the other.
Cofunction: sin θ = cos(90° − θ) — complements trade sine for cosine.
steps.teaser: Next: what happens when the right angle walks away — the Law of Sines.
